The PR persists inbound replay guards for Discord, LINE, and Mattermost, adds bounded WhatsApp durable inbound replay/dead-letter support, exports and documents the shared Plugin SDK helper, and updates tests and SDK baselines.

PR surface: Source +223, Tests +313, Docs +71, Generated 0, Other 0. Total +607 across 20 files.

target.title: fix: inbound messages can be reprocessed after gateway restart or reconnect (persistent replay dedupe + bounded durable replay)
target.body:
Fixes #97538
Part of #69208

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inbound messages could be **reprocessed after a gateway restart or channel reconnect**, producing duplicate agent runs and, in the worst case, an unrecoverable re-delivery storm:

- **Discord / LINE / Mattermost**: the inbound replay dedupe guard was memory-only, so any event the platform re-delivers across a restart (Discord gateway resume, LINE webhook retry, Mattermost websocket replay) was processed again as a fresh message. Sibling channels (Telegram, iMessage, Nextcloud Talk) already persist this guard.
- **WhatsApp (#97538, Bug 2)**: the durable inbound journal replayed *all* pending events on every reconnect with no attempt accounting, no cap, and no dead-letter (pending TTL: 30 days). A poison event — e.g. a heavy multimodal batch whose run stalls before `complete()` — re-delivered on every reconnect forever, and restarting the gateway (the intuitive remediation) re-triggered the storm.

#97538's **Bug 1** (`abort_embedded_run` with `released=0`, owner lock never freed) is the same defect as #91700 and was already fixed by #91802 (`f194be19e2`, shipped in v2026.6.10/v2026.6.11); the reporter was on v2026.6.5. With Bug 1 fixed, the remaining live defect on `main` was the unbounded replay this PR removes. Asks 3 (ingress drain/ack CLI verb) and 4 (replay age threshold) from #97538 are operator/product decisions left to maintainers.

## Why This Change Was Made

One theme: **inbound accept must be idempotent and bounded across restarts**, enforced at the existing chokepoints instead of per-channel patches.

- The three memory-only channels flip to the existing SDK persistent claimable dedupe (`createClaimableDedupe` with `pluginId`/`namespacePrefix`), exactly the shape Telegram/iMessage already use. TTLs and in-memory caps are preserved per channel.
- The durable inbound receive journal (C3 chokepoint, `src/channels/message/durable-receive.ts`) gains its missing terminal state — `fail()` (queue-backed: proper `failed` tombstone via the ingress queue; store-backed: terminal tombstone) — and a canonical `replayPendingDurableInboundReceives({ journal, maxAttempts, process })` helper that counts each replay attempt *before* processing (so stalls and crashes still converge), skips records whose row vanished between the pending snapshot and the attempt (concurrent complete/prune → no stale double-delivery), isolates per-record processing errors (one poison record cannot starve the rest of the pass), and dead-letters at the cap. WhatsApp's inline replay loop is deleted in favor of the helper (`WHATSAPP_DURABLE_INBOUND_MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS = 5`, a bound on total delivery attempts). No new config surface; the shared `channel_ingress_events` queue already had `attempts` and `fail()` — WhatsApp just never used them (Telegram's ingress spool already does).
- The three flipped guards wire `onDiskError` warning logs (persistent dedupe fails open on storage errors; without the hook a broken state DB silently downgrades to memory-only), matching the telegram/nextcloud-talk/raft precedent.
- Test infrastructure: persistent dedupe means suites that reuse fixed message ids need per-test state isolation (`--isolate=false` safety). A shared `installIsolatedPluginStateDirForTests` helper (SDK test runtime) replaces per-suite hand-rolled scaffolds and is applied to the five affected suites, including `message-handler.bot-self-filter.test.ts` which was committing fixed ids through the real guard.

Non-goals: the ingress drain/ack operator verb and reconnect age-threshold policy (asks 3/4 of #97538), and the stale-claim startup sweep (#90989 covers that separately).

Overlap disclosure: open PR #86577 pursues the same intent for the Discord slice (persist the inbound replay guard) but via a file-backed state dir, which predates the plugin-state SQLite migration and conflicts with the current "SQLite only" storage policy; it has failing CI and is waiting on author. This PR covers that surface with the canonical SQLite plugin-state path (the same shape Telegram/iMessage use). If this lands, #86577 should be closed as superseded.

## User Impact

- Discord, LINE, and Mattermost users no longer receive duplicate agent replies when the platform re-delivers an inbound event across a gateway restart.
- WhatsApp deployments can no longer wedge into the #97538 restart-amplified re-delivery loop: a pending inbound event is replayed at most 5 times across reconnects, then dead-lettered with a warning log (`dropping durable WhatsApp inbound after max replay attempts`), keeping the lane healthy. Successfully processed events are unaffected (they complete as before and never replay).

## Evidence

- TDD: every fix landed RED→GREEN.
  - `extensions/discord/src/monitor/inbound-dedupe.test.ts`, `extensions/line/src/webhook-replay-persist.test.ts`, `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/inbound-replay-persist.test.ts`: a committed replay key on a fresh guard instance (= restart) now reports `duplicate` (fails on memory-only guards).
  - `src/channels/message/durable-receive.test.ts` (+6): `fail()` dead-letters on both journal flavors and blocks re-accept; bounded replay processes fresh records, records attempts across stalled replays (`attempts` 1 → 2 → dead-letter at cap), dead-letters poison events, isolates a throwing record while still replaying the rest, and skips a record whose row vanished before the attempt was recorded.
- Suites (post-rebase onto `upstream/main`): WhatsApp **986/986**, Discord **1832/1832**, LINE **292/292**, `src/channels/message/` **171/171**, `src/plugin-state/` **34/34**; mattermost green except `client.retry.test.ts`, which fails identically on the branch base (pre-existing, unrelated HTTP-retry suite).
- `pnpm build` clean; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; `plugin-sdk:api:check` OK (baseline regenerated for the new exports); oxfmt/oxlint clean.
- An 8-angle multi-agent self-review ran on the branch; accepted findings (release-return guard, poison-record isolation, `onDiskError` logging, test state-dir isolation, SDK-surface trims, API baseline) are fixed in the final commit.
- `codex review --base upstream/main` ran locally (per CONTRIBUTING); its single P2 finding — adding a required `fail` method to the shipped `DurableInboundReceiveJournal` SDK type would break external implementers — is addressed: the shipped type is untouched and both factories now return a `DurableInboundReceiveReplayableJournal` intersection that carries `fail`.
- Import-boundary inventories clean (`check-src-extension-import-boundary`, `check-sdk-package-extension-import-boundary` both `[]`); `pnpm test:contracts` 955 passed with 2 failures under triage as pre-existing (evidence below if confirmed).
- Pre-existing, unrelated failure noted for reviewers: `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-shared.test.ts` (2 tests, native streaming usage compat) fails standalone with impl+test byte-identical to base `6cb82eaab8`.
- Known follow-ups deliberately not in this PR: persistent-dedupe per-message SQLite write cost is the same as the existing telegram/imessage guards (amortizing the eviction sweep is a separate perf change); the journal facade's prune-per-release/complete transaction amplification predates this PR; `createClaimableDedupe` defaults `stateMaxEntries` to 1 when omitted (all callers here pass it explicitly).
- SDK contract: `DurableInboundReceiveJournal` (`accept`/`pending`/`complete`/`release`, now `fail`) was already public API through `channel-outbound` — WhatsApp's inbound monitor consumes it from that exact barrel pre-dating this PR. This PR documents the full facade (`docs/plugins/sdk-channel-outbound.md`, "Durable Inbound Receive" section, including "don't build a channel-local dedupe/spool" guidance) and regenerates `docs/docs_map.md`. This is also the intended next step for other channels: Telegram's `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-spool.ts` reimplements the same accept/attempt/dead-letter shape as a channel-local spool and is still accumulating bespoke fixes (as recently as 2 days before this PR) rather than converging on the shared journal — no open PR proposes that consolidation, so keeping this documented and public now avoids reopening the same surface-budget/docs conversation per channel.

**Real gateway restart-replay proof (LINE)** (details + logs in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99365#issuecomment-4872867728)): on a real local gateway built from this branch (isolated `$HOME`, LINE channel, signed webhooks), event `m-proof-1` was delivered and processed, the gateway process was killed and restarted, and the platform-style redelivery of the same event was **deduped across the restart** (`line: skipped replayed webhook event message:m-proof-1`) while a fresh event was processed normally; both replay keys are visible in `plugin_state_entries` (`line.webhook-replay.*`).

Discord and Mattermost flip the exact same shared SDK mechanism (`createClaimableDedupe` with `pluginId`/`namespacePrefix`) that LINE's live proof exercises — only the channel-specific admission/webhook wrapper differs. An equivalent live-gateway demo was attempted for both and is not included here:
- **Discord**: not practically reproducible without a live bot account — its inbound transport is a persistent WebSocket the process opens *outward* to Discord's real servers, so there is no local endpoint to POST a forged redelivery to.
- **Mattermost**: technically reproducible (baseUrl/token are plugin config, so a local fake Mattermost server can stand in), but the attempt hit an unrelated dev-harness artifact (`scripts/run-node.mjs` hot-reloads the channel plugin ~10s after startup even on a fresh build, racing the test push against the reload) rather than a product-code issue.

Both channels have their own real, SQLite-backed regression tests exercising the identical persistent guard through the actual channel handler (not a mock): `extensions/discord/src/monitor/inbound-dedupe.test.ts` and `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.bot-self-filter.test.ts` (drives the real `createDiscordMessageHandler`), and `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/inbound-replay-persist.test.ts`.

**Real cross-process proof of the WhatsApp bounded-replay fix.** WhatsApp's durable-inbound replay trigger is local (it fires on socket attach against on-disk pending state, not on a live platform round-trip), so this mechanism was exercised directly with the actual shipped code from this branch — `src/channels/message/durable-receive.ts` and the exact `WHATSAPP_DURABLE_INBOUND_MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS` constant from `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/durable-receive.ts`, imported and run, not mocked — as **3 separate `node` process invocations**, each with its own module state, against one real on-disk SQLite state dir. This models 3 separate gateway reconnects, including a genuine process kill mid-turn:

Setup (seed): one healthy pending record (`healthy-1`) and one "poison" record (`poison-1`) pre-advanced to `attempts=4` — the exact pre-storm state #97538 describes (a backlog that has already survived several failed reconnect replays).

*Reconnect 1* (new process): `healthy-1` processes and completes normally. `poison-1`'s handler is made to hang forever (models #97538 Bug 1's wedged `embedded_run` lane) — the process is killed via a 3s timeout instead of waiting forever, the same way a real gateway restart would end a wedged run:
```
[phase 1] force-exiting after 3s (simulated crash while poison-1 was wedged)
```
SQLite after the kill: `healthy-1|completed|1`, `poison-1|pending|5`. The attempt was counted (4→5) *before* the crash, because `release()` runs before `process()` in the bounded-replay helper — a stall still converges on the cap instead of resetting the count.

*Reconnect 2* (new process): `poison-1` is now at the cap and is dead-lettered without ever calling its handler again — no further storm:
```
[phase 2] dropping durable WhatsApp inbound after max replay attempts: id=poison-1 attempts=5
[phase 2] pending after replay: []
```

*Reconnect 3* (new process): stays dead — pending is empty, and a simulated platform redelivery of the same id (WhatsApp commonly resends via multi-device/offline sync) is recognized as already-terminal and not reprocessed:
```
[phase 3] redelivery of dead-lettered poison-1 => kind=pending duplicate=true
```
Final state: `healthy-1|completed|1`, `poison-1|failed|5` — the healthy message delivered normally throughout, the poison message stopped storming after exactly 5 total attempts and never came back.

#97538 Bug 1 provenance for reviewers: `f194be19e2` ("fix(diagnostics): release wedged session lane when stuck recovery aborts with queued session work", #91802, fixes #91700) is contained in v2026.6.10+ (`gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/compare/v2026.6.10...f194be19e2` → `behind`).
